t.E920.agn: When JECFA evaluated it as a flavouring substance in 2004, it noted that the amount taken in from foods is many times greater than that expected from flavouring use and saw no safety concern at current levels of intake.
t.E920.body: It is absorbed during digestion and built into the body's proteins; any excess is metabolised and excreted.
t.E920.eval: A flour treatment agent (amino acid). In the EU authorised in flour at quantum satis (as much as needed) and in biscuits for infants and young children up to 1,000 mg/kg. The EU specification (231/2012) prohibits the use of human hair as a source and does not specify any other raw material; it may therefore be of animal origin.
t.E920.found.1: Biscuits for infants and young children (max. 1,000 mg/kg)
t.E920.prod: Formerly obtained by hydrolysis of keratins such as hair; today mostly produced by fermentation or enzymatically; the EU specification prohibits the use of human hair as a source.
t.E920.regx.0: Only in flour (quantum satis) and in biscuits for infants and young children (max. 1,000 mg/kg); human hair may not be used as a source.
t.E920.regx.1: As a flavouring substance, no safety concern at current intake.
t.E920.summary: An amino acid. A flour treatment agent that softens dough; in the EU it may not be produced from human hair.
t.E920.what: An amino acid; as a flour treatment agent it softens dough. One of the natural building blocks of proteins.
